source.title: Dorsal tegmental dopamine neurons gate associative learning of fear

confidence_rationale: This paper identifies a dopaminergic circuit -- ventral periaqueductal gray / dorsal raphe neurons projecting to central amygdala -- that is functionally and anatomically distinct from the canonical VTA reward-coding dopamine population, and shows it encodes a positive prediction error specifically for UNPREDICTED AVERSIVE events (shocks), gating fear-learning plasticity in the amygdala via dopamine-dependent LTP. This is close to direct measurement evidence for MECH-069's E3 (harm/goal error) being carried by a channel dissociable from reward-coding dopamine circuits, rather than the same RPE machinery merely being read out differently downstream -- the aversive-event teaching signal here has its own dedicated anatomical module (PAG/DR->CeA), separate from VTA->striatum. Confidence is moderate-high: strong causal circuit-mapping evidence for a distinct harm/threat channel, but it is a single dopaminergic subpopulation study in mice and does not itself address the E1-vs-E2 side of MECH-069's partition.
failure_signatures: The mechanism reported (positive prediction error for unpredicted shock, dopamine-dependent LTP in amygdala) is itself a prediction-error / reinforcement-learning-shaped signal -- structurally similar in FORM to VTA reward-coding dopamine, even though it is anatomically separate and carries opposite-valence content. A reader could argue this shows the brain reuses one general-purpose dopaminergic prediction-error COMPUTATION across multiple distinct anatomical modules, rather than showing that harm error is a fundamentally different KIND of computation from reward error -- which would weaken MECH-069's incommensurability framing even while supporting its channel-SEPARATION framing.

This is a fear-conditioning (shock) paradigm in mice, not REE's harm/goal-error construct (E3 + residue field, gated by trajectory commitment) -- the mapping from 'aversive Pavlovian US prediction error' to REE's outcome-level, trajectory-gated harm/goal error is not one-to-one.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A dopaminergic circuit distinct from canonical VTA reward-coding dopamine neurons -- originating in ventral periaqueductal gray/dorsal raphe and projecting to central amygdala -- encodes positive prediction errors specifically for unpredicted aversive (shock) events, and this signal gates associative fear learning via dopamine-dependent synaptic plasticity in the amygdala, with negative feedback from central amygdala limiting reinforcement once the aversive event becomes predicted.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-069 claims the harm/goal-error channel (E3 + residue) is incommensurable with sensory (E1) and motor (E2) error and indexes a fundamentally different kind of fidelity -- ethical/purposive rather than world- or motor-model fidelity. Groessl et al. supply anatomical and causal evidence for a genuinely separate neuromodulatory module dedicated to aversive-outcome prediction error, distinct from the canonical reward-coding dopamine system that E1/E2-adjacent literature (Engelhard 2019, Engel 2024, this directory) concerns. This directly supports the existence of a dissociable harm/threat-specific teaching-signal channel, which is the E3 arm of MECH-069's three-way partition.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The signal reported is still prediction-error-shaped (a positive PE for unpredicted shock) and dopamine-carried, so this is better read as evidence for anatomical/functional MODULE separation (a distinct harm-signaling circuit exists) than as evidence that harm error is COMPUTATIONALLY incommensurable with reward-error in the strong sense MECH-069's text uses ('cannot be derived from or collapsed into another without loss'). It is also a Pavlovian fear-conditioning paradigm, not REE's trajectory-gated, outcome-level E3+residue construct.
mapping.source_context: Mouse; optogenetic/electrophysiological circuit mapping of PAG/DR dopaminergic projections to central amygdala; Pavlovian fear conditioning with unpredicted foot-shock US.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality causal circuit-mapping study in a strong venue, directly on point for the 'is there a dedicated harm/threat teaching-signal channel' question. Mapping fidelity moderate: strong for the anatomical-separation claim, weaker for the strict incommensurability claim, since the underlying computation is still prediction-error-shaped.
